Los Angeles slipped to 2-3 after an overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills where they had a game-winning field goal blocked. It is hardly a record befitting the supposed favorites for the Super Bowl, regardless of whether they have been missing key players like Myles Garrett or not. And it was no surprise when Sean McVay described how angry both he and the team were in the wake of their most recent defeat. However, the situation is by no means a disaster for the Rams. For one, the latest Super Bowl odds listed by sportsbooks still have them at +700 to be crowned champions in February 2027, with only Buffalo having shorter odds among some operators. item.description: Kentucky Basketball is definitely back, and the season opener against Little Rock went about as well as it could have from a health standpoint. Nobody got hurt, and that was probably the best thing I can say about a performance that was more concerning than I would have anticipated. Credit to former Kentucky great Travis Ford, though. He had his team ready to battle, and the Trojans made Kentucky work for it all night long. The Cats got the win, but there were enough issues to make this a more interesting opener than anyone probably wanted. From turnovers to defensive potential, there is plenty to take away from the first game of the season. Here are three things to look at after Kentucky’s 69-49 win. 1. Turnovers were a problem I brought this up previously when discussing the pairing of Zoom Diallo and Alex Wilkins, but I didn’t expect Little Rock to be the team to drive that point home. At one point in the second half, the TV announcers said that Kentucky looked like it had never seen a press before. Not exactly a ringing endorsement, and certainly not something you want to hear about a team with this much talent playing a team like Little Rock. Diallo and Wilkins combined for 7 turnovers and 6 assists. As a team, Kentucky finished with 19 turnovers and just 12 assists. Some of that low assist total can be attributed to missed shots, but the turnover numbers are still concerning. The bigger issue is how easily the Trojans were able to disrupt Kentucky’s offense. item.title: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer reacts to Eagles signing Joe Milton amid Jalen Hurts’ blood clot
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer reacts to Eagles signing Joe Milton amid Jalen Hurts’ blood clot appeared first on ClutchPoints . Coach Brian Schottenheimer ’s 2-3 Dallas Cowboys are planning to welcome Green Bay for a Week 6 tilt that raised a Jerry Jones-answered question about whether Dallas is wasting Dak Prescott’s prime years . Coach Brian Schottenheimer’s recent Christian Parker revelation revealed that he is at odds with Jones with the Cowboys one week away from a showdown against Nick Sirianni’s Eagles. Schottenheimer spoke to media about the Eagles’ decision to sign former Cowboys fan favorite, and former Tennessee Volunteers and Michigan Wolverines quarterback, Joe Milton off the team’s practice squad in light of Jalen Hurts’ scary blood clot issue . “I think it’s a great opportunity for Joe,” Schottenheimer said. “They recognize this is a young man with incredible talent. I think the world of Joe, so I’m sad to see him go. I hope he gets every opportunity.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Milton has played in five NFL games, including four with the Cowboys, compiling 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He has one of the NFL’s strongest arms, although his accuracy and decision making have been works-in-progress. He will now have an opportunity to learn from Hurts, Tanner McKee and Sirianni on an Eagles team that has been struggling with injuries as of late. Schottenheimer’s Cowboys are hoping to score an upset victory over the Packers with star receiver CeeDee Lamb giving an encouraging injury update recently . The Cowboys, and their head coach, will miss Milton, but the Eagles offer a chance for him to learn from some of the best offensive minds in the NFL. Dallas fans will likely continue to root for him, at least when he’s not playing their team, in the foreseeable future as the NFL season continues. item.title: New Penguins Defenseman Ryan Johnson Reveals What He Can Bring to Pittsburgh
item.description: New Penguins Defenseman Ryan Johnson Reveals What He Can Bring to Pittsburgh originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ryan Johnson hasn't made his Pittsburgh Penguins debut yet, but the defenseman already has an idea of how he can contribute to his new team. Acquired from the Buffalo Sabres on Oct. 12, Johnson brings NHL experience and a puck-moving skill set to Pittsburgh's defensive line. The 25-year-old discussed his strengths in an interview with SportsNet Pittsburgh's Katie Florio. "Just the ability to distribute the puck and break pucks out, can contribute to the offense too." Ryan Johnson on how he can contribute to this Penguins team and reuniting with fellow California kid Nick Robertson ⬇️ 🎤 @KatieFlorio https://t.co/2zYQSbSVP9 — SportsNet Pittsburgh (@SNPittsburgh) October 17, 2026 "Defensively, I think that's my strength where I can use my feet, speed, quickness too to play fast and try to help get the team the puck," Johnson said. His ability to move the puck and defend with his skating could give Pittsburgh another option on the blue line as he works toward earning a spot in the lineup. Johnson has appeared in 47 career NHL games, all with Buffalo, recording seven assists. He played a career-high 41 games during the 2023-24 season but spent much of the following two campaigns in the American Hockey League. Johnson played for the Rochester Americans, Buffalo's AHL affiliate, throughout his first three-plus professional seasons. He also began the 2026-27 campaign there, appearing in four games before the trade to Pittsburgh. The defenseman said the AHL's competitive pace and the opportunity to play significant minutes helped him continue developing his game. He believes those experiences will benefit him as he looks to earn another opportunity in the NHL. Now with Pittsburgh, Johnson is getting acquainted with his new teammates while waiting for his opportunity to enter the lineup. He said the chance to practice with the Penguins and spend time around the group has made the transition enjoyable. "It's been actually fun to just meet the guys here and get ready into the action too," Johnson said. "Watching the game and then practicing with the guys too. It's been nice." item.title: Framber Valdez's longtime catcher reportedly joining Tigers' staff
item.description: DETROIT — The Tigers' coaching staff is getting a new face. But it's a familiar face for manager AJ Hinch and starting pitcher Framber Valdez. Martin Maldonado, who was a catcher in the major leagues for 15 seasons, including two impactful stints with the Houston Astros , will be the Tigers' new quality-control coach, according to multiple reports Friday, Oct. 16. The Athletic first reported Maldonado's hiring , and MLB.com confirmed the hiring. The Tigers have not yet publicly announced any coaching-staff changes since the end of the regular season. Maldonado, 40, played for seven teams during his major-league career, including the Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Angels, Kansas City Royals, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres. He retired from the major leagues after the 2025 season, though he did play for Puerto Rico in the 2026 World Baseball Classic. The Tigers' job will be his first major-league coaching job. He was a special assistant with the Atlanta Braves in 2026. Maldonado first played for the Astros in 2018, under Hinch, after being acquired at that year's trade deadline. He left as a free agent the following offseason, but he rejoined the Astros ahead of the trade deadline in July 2019 and stayed with Houston through the 2023 season. The Astros made the playoffs all six years Maldonado was in Houston, and he was part of the 2023 team that won the World Series. A career .203/.277/.343 hitter, Maldonado made his biggest impact on the defensive side of the ball. He won a Gold Glove in 2017 while playing for the Angels. Maldonado also caught Valdez for 91 games — more than twice as many as any of Valdez's other catchers — including two of the lefty's best seasons in the majors, 2022 and 2023. He caught three no-hitters with the Astros, including Valdez's in 2023, so there's surely a comfort factor there between the two. And certainly, it's worth noting Valdez that had his ups and downs with the Tigers in 2026, the first year of a three-year, $115-million contract. He had a 4.03 ERA and 1.362 WHIP, both the highest of his career since he became a full-time starter in 2020. Opponents had a .702 OPS against Valdez in 2026; their OPS when Maldonado caught him was .631. Maldonado will fill the Tigers' quality-control coach job that previously was held by Billy Boyer, who was promoted to third-base coach in July after Joey Cora suddenly and surprisingly parted ways with Hinch . It was previously reported this offseason that the Tigers are parting ways assistant pitching coach Juan Nieves and first-base coach Anthony Sanders , as well as head athletic trainer Ryne Eubanks and assistant trainer Chris McDonald. tpaul@detroitnews.com @tonypaul1984 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Framber Valdez's longtime catcher reportedly joining Tigers' staff

item.title: Joaquin Buckley gives corniest UFC interview you’ve seen ahead of Edmonton main event
item.description: The Ultimate Fighting Championship is in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, this weekend for UFC Fight Night 291 at the Rogers Place. In the main event, Joaquin Buckley faces off against Mike Malott at welterweight. On Friday night, the ceremonial weigh-ins took place with both fighters coming face-to-face one final time before Saturday night’s throwdown. After hitting the scale and facing off, Buckley met with UFC correspondant McKenzie Pavacich for an interview. That’s when Buckley went mute and did not speak during the entire interview. On stage, Buckley refused to shake UFC boss Dana White’s hand, so following it up with a silent interview drew some criticism from the fans. From fans calling him a “clown” trying to be like Gable Steveson or Jon Jones to simply calling him out for corny behavior, fans weren’t feeling the “locked in” gimmick. MORE: UFC Edmonton fight card & weigh-in results for Joaquin Buckley vs Mike Malott Joaquin Buckley Gives Silent Interview “Well, Joaquin, you said it yourself, Fight Week is a celebration of all the hard work. You are so locked in right now. How have the celebrations been this week?,” Pavacich said to crickets. “All right, I think that says more than any words could. Now, third UFC main event, how much confidence do you bring from the previous ones that you’ve had? Now, this one, not necessarily enemy territory. “You spoke this week about how it’s not really something that applies to you. You are able to connect with people all over the world. You’re able to really enjoy these weeks. What do you think the crowd will be like tomorrow? This might be a first for me, guys. Joaquin, we will let you stay locked in, get ready for this fight. Best of luck to you. Guys, we’ll send it back to you.” MORE: Dana White savagely roasts Contender Series fighter before awarding UFC contract It’s disrespectful and a played out gimimck, but fighters need to do whatever they can to get in their zone and hype themselves up. However, for Buckley, he’s going to need to put on a show and come away with a quick knockout, or the memes and clowning will be endless. UFC Edmonton is set to kick off at 5:00 p.m. ET with the preliminary card, before the main card begins at 8:00 p.m. ET with a lightweight scrap between Nate Landwehr and Mandel Nallo. item.title: ESPN will reportedly pay additional $345 million annually for expanded College Football Playoff
item.description: Credit: Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect On Thursday, ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported that the College Football Playoff was “ nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams ,” beginning with the 2027 season. This may sound hyperbolic, but it’s not: Nearly everyone hated the news, though nobody hates it more than Josh Pate . Amidst the backlash, Nick Saban called a spade a spade . “The bottom line is money,” Saban said on The Pat McAfee Show on Friday morning. By Friday night, Thamel reported the eye-popping financial terms. “Sources: The average additional payment that ESPN will pay for the expanded college football playoff is $345 million annually the next five years, which is in addition to the average of $1.3 billion annually over that time ESPN is already paying,” Thamel posted to X . In a separate post, Thamel wrote , “Of that new $345 million, ESPN will only essentially be paying $205 million, as they are getting back $140 million annually from the cancelation of the three power conference championship games that ESPN owns the television rights to broadcast.” Around the time of Thamel’s reporting, ESPN’s Heather Dinich reported that the College Football Playoff reached “a handshake agreement” with ESPN to broadcast the presumptive 24-team playoff. “Though there is still a significant amount of work to be done on paper, and everything is still subject to board approval across all involved parties, the agreement is a significant step closer to doubling the postseason path to the national title for next year,” Dinich wrote. ESPN holds sole media rights to the College Football Playoff, most recently agreeing to a six-year, $7.8 billion contract in March 2024, as reported by Dinich at the time. The current deal runs through the 2031-32 season. There are still plenty of moving parts, at least outwardly. But no sport loves change for the sake of change (and money) more than college football, and yet another seismic shift seems destined to rock college football next year. item.title: Joe Willock Future Takes New Twist as Besiktas Interest Remains
item.description: COVENTRY, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 12: Joe Willock of Newcastle United during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Coventry City and Newcastle United at The Coventry Building Society Arena on October 12, 2026 in Coventry, England. (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joe Willock appeared to have played his way firmly into Matthias Jaissle’s plans after Newcastle United rejected Besiktas’ summer approach and the midfielder responded with three goals in his first seven appearances of the season. However, Daily Mail’s Craig Hope reported that the outlook on Willock’s Newcastle future has changed significantly, with no extension currently close despite earlier expectations that the 27-year-old would sign a new deal. “On the subject of contracts, Confidential understands nothing is close when it comes to Joe Willock,” Hope reported. “There was an expectation he would also sign an extension after Newcastle rejected an approach from Besiktas in the summer. That, however, is now less certain.” Willock’s existing contract expires next summer, meaning he can sign a pre-contract agreement with a foreign club from January. Besiktas remains interested after president Serdal Adalı previously confirmed the Turkish club intends to return for the former Arsenal midfielder. item.title: Meet the team: Yusef Gray Jr.
item.description: West Allis Central's Yusef Gray Jr. (3) breaks past Wayzata's Nolen Anderson (3) during the Rick Majerus WBY Shootout on Monday, Dec. 29, 2025, at Concordia University in Mequon, Wisconsin. Wayzata won the game, 67-64. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co One of the biggest developments in last year’s squads was the large involvement of the freshman class. The trio of Killyan Toure, Jamarion Batemon and Dominykas Pleta were instrumental in maintaining depth across position groups and developing rapidly throughout the season. What kind of impact will the new class of freshman have? Let’s start with Yusef Gray Jr., the latest edition in the Wisconsin to Iowa State pipeline. Gray is listed as a 6-4 point guard, which is on the bigger side for the position (Toure and Tamin Lipsey are 6-3 and 6-1 respectively). Gray is coming off a shoulder injury that cut his senior season short, so his rehab was priority number one throughout the off-season. His defensive prowess has been a calling card for the coaching staff, which should not be a surprise to anyone who has followed the program in recent years. Even with a shortened senior season, Gray still finished as a Wisconsin Mr. Basketball finalist, and chose Iowa State over other P5 offers such as Creighton, Mississippi State, DePaul, and hometown Marquette. In 20 games his senior year, Gray averaged 24.3 points, 6.9 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.1 steals per game while shooting 57.6% from the field. At the high school level, it is difficult to see 57.6% unless it is a center that is just taller than everyone else, so we know that Gray can score. During the non-conference season, we are naturally going to see some unique combinations and more minutes distributed among the roster. This will especially be important for Gray as Toure is out until at least January, and Lipsey’s eligibility will be a question every day. He will still have to battle for minutes with Jaquan “Bully” Johnson and Ryan Prather Jr. Johnson is bringing in hardnosed defense as he earned Missouri Valley Conference Defensive Player of the Year honors, and Prather averaged a career best 15.7 points and 3.6 assists per game at Robert Morris before suffering a hip injury. This is a tough lineup to crack as a newcomer, but who knows what the future holds. I don’t think anyone could have properly predicted the impact that Toure, Batemon, and Pleta would have during the season, so why not Gray? Regardless of what his role is this season with the Cyclones, he has an incredible opportunity to learn from a very experienced point guard room and TJ’s squad. He also has the opportunity to wow us during the non-conference season and earn quality minutes even with a (hopefully) deep point guard depth chart.

The Dallas Stars are coming off a win against the Colorado Avalanche. The win was a big one for Dallas, who had lost two straight contests. However, the team felt they needed to add some more depth to the roster. As a result, they elected to sign veteran winger David Perron . Perron was a free agent the entire summer after splitting last season between the Ottawa Senators and Detroit Red Wings. He is now returning to the league for his 20th NHL season. On Friday, Stars head coach Glen Gulutzan explained why his team elected to make this move. “We watched him (Thursday),” Gulutzan said, via NHL.com. “Obviously the veteran presence is there and his actual play, just how good he is along the walls. He’s heavy and hard on pucks, he has a huge hockey IQ, he’s competitive and that’s the reason we got him.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Perron has become a solid bottom-six winger over the last few years. The veteran winger has struggled with some injuries as well. Last season, he played 65 games, scoring 13 goals and 28 points. The Stars are without center Matt Duchene for a few months. He has undergone core muscle surgery and is currently recovering from the procedure. Perron is not a center by trade, but does give the team depth at forward while Duchene is out. Gulutzan noted that the veteran winger will not be with the Stars on Saturday due to visa issues. However, they do expect him in the lineup once he’s up to speed. The Stars will look for a second straight win on Saturday when they take on the Chicago Blackhawks. item.title: Bucks Announce Major News for Home Opener
item.description: Bucks Getty The Milwaukee Bucks have announced major news for the team’s home opener, which is set to take place on October 23. The Bucks are set to open the 2026-27 NBA season at home against the Chicago Bulls on Friday, October 23. Originally, the game was set to begin at 7 p.m. CT, but with the Milwaukee Brewers playing in the World Series that night, the Bucks decided to move up their home opener to 3 p.m. CT instead, giving Milwaukee sports fans the opportunity to watch both of their teams play sports that day. Bucks Move Up Home Opener Taking to their social media, the Bucks released an official statement about the time change for their home opener against the rival Bulls. “The Brewers’ return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin. Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we’ll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run. The Los Angeles Dodgers were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, leading to an “a**-kicking” admission by an MLB reporter . Long answer short, the Dodgers are built to last. Freddie Freeman (37 years old), Mookie Betts (34), and Blake Snell (33) are a few of the Dodgers’ top players in their 30s as they head toward winter meetings. item.title: Broncos Star Posts Lengthy Statement After NFL Clears Path to Return
item.description: Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper got a significant update about his legal team. Getty In terms of second chances, this might be the only one Denver Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper gets from the NFL after he was taken off the commissioner’s exempt list and cleared to rejoin his team for a Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals. Cooper was arrested twice in one week this summer and charged with felony domestic violence — the incidents that landed him on the commissioner’s list — and addressed his pending reinstatement with a lengthy statement to his official Instagram account. “Playing in the NFL and representing the Denver Broncos is a privilege I do not take for granted,” Cooper wrote on Friday. “I’m grateful to ownership, my teammates, coaches and everyone in the organization for their support as well as Commissioner Goodell and the league for the opportunity to return. Over the last several months, I’ve spent a lot of time working to better myself. That work will continue. My focus is on being the best person, father, teammate and member of this community I can be. I will show that commitment through my actions every day. Praise God – thank you Jesus.” Cooper also seemed to address his return on his Instagram stories, where he posted a meme with the words “Jesus wins, every single time.” View this post on Instagram Jonathaon Cooper’s Court Date Set for March Friday’s news of Cooper’s return came after he appeared at a Douglas County courthouse on Monday for a motions hearing alongside famed attorney Harvey Steinberg, who is handling his case. Cooper entered a not guilty plea on felony domestic violence charges on August 31 and was placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list, meaning he was not allowed to practice or play for the Broncos while he’s on the list. “In Jonathon Cooper motion hearing, the prosecution asked for continuance,” 9News Denver’s Mike Klis wrote on his official X account on Monday. “Steinberg asked for speedy trial, set for March 2-4. Motion hearing on Feb 23. Cooper will be allowed to travel in case cleared from commissioners list.” Cooper’s second arrest came for violating a protection order from the 1st arrest. “With Jonathon Cooper’s trial now pushed to March, when was the last time a player came off the NFL commissioner’s exempt list with a trial date still looming?” Broncos reporter Rachel Vigil wrote on her official X account on Monday. “ Jabrill Peppers , 2024. Seven games on paid leave, then reinstated before his case ended. The difference: Peppers wasn’t facing a felony. Cooper is.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Broncos Star Posts Lengthy Statement After NFL Clears Path to Return appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?
item.description: Pundits regularly criticise teams for not running enough but is there a link between distance covered and results? By Opta Analyst It was like clockwork. Manchester United dropped points against Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical statistics to make points. Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Manchester United.” Continue reading...

item.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
item.description: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations. Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea are the Premier League’s most fun team but is it sustainable?
item.description: Xabi Alonso’s side are scoring and conceding at a remarkable rate. It’s great for neutrals but not necessarily the best way to qualify for Europe By WhoScored Watching Chelsea this season ought to come with a health warning. Goals arrive in abundance, leads are established before spectators have settled into their seats and clean sheets have become an alien concept. Xabi Alonso has transformed Chelsea into one of the Premier League’s most thrilling spectacles. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 13. That’s 4.7 goals per game in six matches. Chelsea are a neutral’s dream, but is it sustainable? They have scored 15 goals from an expected goals total of just 8.4, an over-performance of 6.6. Their 18.3% conversion rate is second only to Manchester City’s 19.1%, while eight of their 15 goals have come from shots with xG below 0.13. item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. item.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
item.description: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. It was an amazing way to go out on a high.” Five months later McKenna has no regrets about electing to cut things short while the going was so good. The golf bag lying outside his garage speaks of a man enjoying the break and, more pertinently, of something bigger. His son has recently become interested in the sport and sharing those moments with loved ones, whether out on the greens or spending part of the summer travelling along the East Anglian coastline in a camper van, were among the biggest reasons to pause a soaring career. At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...

At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
